title: Local magnetic properties of the rare-earth intermetallics $R$Mn$_2$Ge$_2$ ($R$=Ce, Pr, Nd)
authors: N. P. Bentley, T. L. Breeze, A. Hernández-Melián, M. J. Pearce, T. J. Hicken, M. T. F. Telling, B. M. Huddart, D. A. Mayoh, G. Balakrishnan, S. J. Clark, T. Lancaster
abstract: We present an investigation of the rare-earth intermetallic materials, $R$Mn$_2$Ge$_2$ ($R$=Ce, Pr, Nd), reported to host a lattice of skyrmionic bubbles at room temperature. The magnetism of all three materials is characterised by the onset of local fluctuations as the magnetic state changes from a conical magnetic structure to a collinear antiferromagnetic one as temperature $T$ is increased. In this $T$ regime, where skyrmion-bubble textures have been reported, we see dynamics similar to those observed in other skyrmion-hosting materials. The level of disorder above this transition increases across the series from $R$=Ce to Nd. At low temperatures the magnetism is affected by the ordering of the rare-earth ions, resulting in distinct behaviour for the different members of the series.
summary: This work characterizes the temperature-dependent local magnetism in RMn2Ge2 intermetallics using muon spin spectroscopy. By analyzing magnetic transitions from conical to antiferromagnetic phases, the authors map out how rare-earth ion ordering and crystal symmetry dictate the material's exotic magnetic behavior. The combination of $\mu$SR measurements and DFT calculations provides a detailed picture of local spin dynamics in these correlated systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the local magnetic properties of rare-earth intermetallic compounds RMn2Ge2, focusing on their temperature-dependent magnetic transitions and skyrmion hosting.
main_result: Muon spin spectroscopy reveals distinct magnetic phases (conical to collinear AFM) across the series, with disorder increasing from Ce to Nd. The local magnetism is strongly influenced by rare-earth ion ordering at low temperatures.
method: The research combines experimental measurements using Muon Spin Rotation ($\mu$SR) with theoretical calculations employing Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Crystal Field Hamiltonian analysis.
model_or_system: The physical system is the rare-earth intermetallic compounds RMn2Ge2 (R=Ce, Pr, Nd). The magnetism involves transitions between conical and collinear antiferromagnetic structures, which are probed by local magnetic field measurements.
key_observables: Muon asymmetry A(t), precession frequency $\nu(T)$, local magnetic fields $|B|$, and energy level splittings $\Delta \text{CEF}$.
important_parameters: Temperature (T) regimes defining phase transitions ($T_c=318$ K, $T_N=417$ K), and the rare-earth element R.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the muon site is crystallographically unique for tracking changes across the series; DFT calculations use specific functionals (PBE).
figures_summary: Figures show rapid oscillatory $\mu$SR spectra below $T_c$, order-parameter-like behavior of frequency vs. temperature, and comparisons between calculated dipolar field distributions at candidate muon sites and measured local fields.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the magnetic transitions using $\mu$SR data across different R elements (Ce, Pr, Nd), correlating observed spectral changes with theoretical predictions derived from DFT calculations of local fields based on assumed magnetic structures.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the use of $\mu$SR to probe local spin dynamics and symmetry breaking in correlated materials provides insights into complex many-body ground states relevant to strongly correlated electron physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. ZF µSR measurements of CeMn2Ge2 demonstrating rapid oscillatory behaviour in the first 0.05 µs of the time window. (a) Asymmetry spectra below Tc = 318 K, with the change in (b) precession frequency and (c) amplitudes, A1 (red circles), A2 (blue squares), and A1 + A2 (green triangles) with temperature. The dotted line at 218 K marks the onset of changes in the amplitudes due to the spin reorientation transition at Tc.

FIG. 2. ZF µSR measurements of CeMn2Ge2 demonstrat- ing relaxing behaviour over 5 µs. (a) Asymmetry spectra at several temperatures, showing the missing asymmetry as- sociated to the oscillating fraction being recovered above Tc. (b) Change in relaxation rate with temperature [with an inset showing the decrease in relaxing amplitude A3 (blue squares)], that occurs between 218 K and Tc (green circles). The fit of Eq. 6 to λ3 is shown in black and the background contribu- tion, A4 (orange triangles), is approximately constant. Above Tc = 318 K both amplitudes are globally refined and held con- stant, and λ3 points are plotted as purple diamonds.

FIG. 3. Dipole field distributions calculated at the muon site for reported incommensurate magnetic orderings in RMn2Ge2 (R=Ce, Pr, Nd), with the muon site shown in the structure of RMn2Ge2 (R=Ce, Pr, Nd). In CeMn2Ge2, the field distribution corresponding to the measured helical magnetic structure [27] at (a) 4 K is shown, with the dotted line corresponding to the precession frequency of 249.0(5) MHz from our µSR measurements. In PrMn2Ge2 the field distributions for the reported magnetic structures [28] at (b) 200 K and (c) 10 are presented. The dotted lines indicate the value of the local field from our µSR measurements, which corresponds to precession frequencies of 209.0(4) MHz at 200 K...

FIG. 4. ZF µSR measurements of PrMn2Ge2. (a) A set of asymmetry spectra, demonstrating the evolution of the oscillations with temperature. (b) Variation of the precession frequency with temperature, fitted with Eq. 8. (c) Temperature dependence of the slow magnetic dynamics (λ3) below Tc (with the fit of Eq. 6 shown in black) and the rapid relaxation of the oscillating term (λ1) above Tc. (d) Variation of oscillating (A1), relaxing (A2) and total amplitude below Tc, demonstrating the swapping of amplitudes between Ticm and Tc.

FIG. 5. Evolution of the early-time spectra of NdMn2Ge2 with temperature, demonstrating the transi- tion to a single frequency above TSR = 215 K that increase in amplitude with spin-reorientation into the a-b plane at higher temperatures.
